column1: # AQL Language Specification: Open words — scoped `def` extension of existing words
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# design/OPEN-WORDS.0.md: `def <word> fn […]` on a word that carries
# LOCKED signatures (every natively registered word) MERGES the fn's
# signatures into a word CLONE bound through the ordinary def shadow
# stack — scoped like every other def (fn body / module body / top
# level), popped by `undef`, inherited by sub-engines, captured by
# closures. Locked signatures sort first in match order, so no
# previously-valid call changes its dispatch; a merge tuple exactly
# matching a locked tuple is refused ([aql/locked_signature]); sealed
# words (def / make / word — the kernel's name-keyed identities) refuse
# entirely ([aql/reserved_word]). A module exports its merged word like
# any other fn (`export "M" {add: add/r}`) and `import` TRANSPLANTS the
# extension one level into the importing registry; re-export is the
# opt-in for transitivity, and the inline-module firewall is the
# opt-out. Plain user fns (no locked sigs) keep whole-replacement
# shadowing — the REPL/iterate idiom.
# §1  the merge — top level
def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  add true false
column3: a merged signature dispatches on the extended word

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  add 1 2
column3: locked native dispatch is unchanged inside the extending scope

column1: def add fn [[a:Integer b:Integer] [Integer] [99]]  add 1 2
column3: locked-first: an unlocked tuple overlapping a locked family can never pre-empt the locked match — previously-valid calls are byte-identical

column1: add true false
column3: an engine without the merge errors exactly as today (negative twin of §1 row 1)

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  do [add true false]
column3: a top-level merge is visible to sub-engines, like any top-level def

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  [false true] each [add true]
column3: higher-order bodies see the merge too

column1: # §2  the merge — fn-body scope (body-local def, torn down at exit)
def f fn [[x:Boolean] [Boolean] [def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]] add x false]]  f true
column3: a fn-body merge extends the word inside the body

column1: def f fn [[x:Boolean] [Boolean] [def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]] add x false]]  (f true) add true false
column3: the body-local merge is INVISIBLE after fn exit (negative twin)

column1: def g fn [[] [Function] [def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]] ([x:Boolean] => [add x false])]]  def h (g)  h true
column3: closure capture: a lambda constructed inside a fn-scoped merge keeps the merge after the scope exits (the uniform closure rule, §4.3)

column1: # §3  locked and sealed refusals
def add fn [[a:Number b:Number] [Number] [a]]
column3: a merge tuple exactly matching a LOCKED signature can never replace it

column1: def def fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]]
column3: `def` is sealed — the kernel relies on its name identity

column1: def make fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]]
column3: `make` is sealed (autoEvalMap gating keys on the name)

column1: def word fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]]
column3: `word` is sealed (splice-paren expansion keys on the name)

column1: def add 42
column3: a NON-fn body on a built-in stays a refused redefinition — only fn merges open the word

column1: undef add
column3: undef of a built-in with no extension present stays refused

column1: # §4  unlocked replacement and undef unwinding
def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a and b]]  add true false
column3: re-merging the same UNLOCKED tuple replaces it in scope

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a and b]]  undef add  add true false
column3: undef pops the replacement, restoring the previous merge

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  undef add  add 1 2
column3: undef pops the merge; the base word is intact

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  undef add  add true false
column3: undef pops the merge; the added tuple is gone (negative twin)

column1: undef add (fnsig [[Number Number] [Number]])  add 1 2
column3: targeted signature-undef never removes a locked (native) signature

column1: def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]]  undef add (fnsig [[Boolean Boolean] [Boolean]])  add true false
column3: targeted signature-undef leaves a word-extension clone intact (it carries locked sigs); plain `undef add` is the retraction

column1: # §5  plain user fns keep whole-replacement shadowing (§4.1)
def f fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [1]]  def f fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [2]]  f 5
column3: re-def of a plain user fn with the same tuple REPLACES it (the REPL idiom) — no merge semantics without locked sigs

column1: # §6  module scope: extending a core word REQUIRES a user type (§4.4b)
# A module may extend a core word only with at least one user-defined
# (non-kernel) argument type per signature. An all-kernel tuple would
# change what core calls mean for every importer (`add 1 {}` suddenly
# working) and breaks forward compatibility the day core claims the
# tuple as a locked signature. Top-level programs are unrestricted
# (§1); external-builtin domain types (Date, Matrix, …) anchor a
# module's signature just like a minted user type.
import module [def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]] export "M" {add: add/r}]
column3: a module cannot extend a core word with an all-core tuple

column1: import module [def add fn [[a:Integer b:Map] [Integer] [1]] export "M" {add: add/r}]
column3: `add 1 {}` can never start working because of an import

column1: import module [def add fn [[a:Boolean b:Boolean] [Boolean] [a or b]] export "M" {x:1}]
column3: refused at the module-body def itself — even a module-PRIVATE all-core extension breaks when core later claims the tuple

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Integer b:Flag] [Boolean] [true]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r}]  add 1 (M.mk true)
column3: a MIXED tuple qualifies — one user type anchors the signature

column1: import module [def add fn [[a:Date b:Date] [Boolean] [true]] export "M" {add: add/r}]  import "aql:time-util"  add TimeUtil.today TimeUtil.today
column3: an external-builtin domain type (Date) anchors a module extension — the §6 migration shape

column1: # §7  export transplant — one level, opt-in transitivity (user-typed)

import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  add (M.mk true) (M.mk true)
column3: exporting the merged word transplants the extension into the importer's bare word

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  add (M.mk true) (M.mk false)
column3: the transplanted body runs (module-closure execution) — not a stub match

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  M.add (M.mk true) (M.mk false)
column3: the namespaced binding exists alongside the transplant (§4.9)

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  add 1 2
column3: locked native dispatch is untouched by a transplant

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  typeof (M.mk true)
column3: the module's minted type crosses the boundary with its values

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  def Flag M.Flag  def x:Flag true  def y:Flag true  add x y
column3: the importer constructs its OWN values via the exported type (alias annotation) and the transplanted signature dispatches on them

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  add (M.mk true) (M.mk true)
column3: a module-body merge WITHOUT an export of the word is module-private — nothing crosses the boundary

column1: import module [import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "I" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}] def Flag I.Flag def omk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "O" {mk: omk/r}]  add (O.mk true) (O.mk true)
column3: one level only: the TYPE crossed two boundaries (O.mk builds Flag-conforming values) but the word extension did not — this is also the firewall idiom

column1: import module [import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "I" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}] def Flag I.Flag def omk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "O" {mk: omk/r add: add/r}]  add (O.mk true) (O.mk true)
column3: re-export is the opt-in for transitivity: the outer module re-exports the word and its importer gains the extension

column1: import module [def add fn [[a:Date b:Date] [Boolean] [true]] export "M" {add: add/r}]  import module [def add fn [[a:Date b:Date] [Boolean] [false]] export "N" {add: add/r}]
column3: the same unlocked tuple arriving from two different modules is a loud conflict (§4.4)

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  def add fn [[a:(M.Flag) b:(M.Flag)] [Boolean] [a or b]]  add (M.mk true) (M.mk false)
column3: a direct user def still replaces a transplanted tuple freely — the conflict rule is module-vs-module only

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  undef add  add 1 2
column3: undef pops the transplant; the base word is intact

column1: import module [def Flag (refine Boolean) def add fn [[a:Flag b:Flag] [Boolean] [a and b]] def mk fn [[b:Boolean] [Flag] [def v:Flag b v]] export "M" {add: add/r mk: mk/r Flag: Flag}]  undef add  add (M.mk true) (M.mk true)
column3: undef pops the transplant; the transplanted tuple is gone (negative twin)

column1: # §8  extending module-provided words
import "aql:math-util"  def sqrt MathUtil.sqrt  def sqrt fn [[s:String] [Integer] [7]]  sqrt "x"
column3: a native-module wrapper rebound to a bare name carries LOCKED sigs, so def merges onto it (§4.1 — module words count); no user-type rule here, the word is not core

column1: import "aql:math-util"  def sqrt MathUtil.sqrt  def sqrt fn [[s:String] [Integer] [7]]  sqrt 16.0
column3: the wrapper's locked signature still dispatches first

column1: import "aql:math-util"  def sqrt MathUtil.sqrt  def sqrt fn [[x:Float] [Float] [1.0]]
column3: the wrapper's locked tuple cannot be replaced, same as a core word's

column1: import module [def w fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [1]] export "B" {w: w/r}]  def w B.w  def w fn [[a:String] [Integer] [2]]  w "s"
column3: a PLAIN module fn (no locked sigs) rebound and re-defd keeps user-word semantics — the new overload dispatches

column1: import module [def w fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [1]] export "B" {w: w/r}]  def w B.w  def w fn [[a:String] [Integer] [2]]  w 5
column3: …and the module fn's own overload stays reachable (cross-stack overloading, not a merge)

column1: import module [import "aql:math-util" def sqrt MathUtil.sqrt def sqrt fn [[s:String] [Integer] [7]] export "M" {sqrt: sqrt/r}]  M.sqrt "x"
column3: a module may extend ANOTHER module's word and export it; with no bare `sqrt` in the importer the export degrades to the namespaced binding (§4.9)
